questions.question: A’s and B’s salaries are respectively 40% and 70% rupees more than C’s salary. What is the ratio of B’s salary to A’s salary?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let C's salary be the base value of 100.

A's salary is 40% more → 140.

B's salary is 70% more → 170.

Required Ratio (B : A) = 170 : 140 = 17 : 14

**∴ The correct answer is 17 : 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A's salary = C's salary + 40%

B's salary = C's salary + 70%

 C
 
 100% (Base)

 A
 
 140% (+40%)

 B
 
 170% (+70%)
 
 Ratio B : A = 170 : 140 = 17 : 14

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let C's salary = x

⇒ A's salary = x + (40/100) × x = 1.4x

⇒ B's salary = x + (70/100) × x = 1.7x

⇒ Ratio of B's salary to A's salary = B / A

⇒ Ratio = 1.7x / 1.4x

⇒ Ratio = 17 / 14 = 17 : 14

**∴ The correct answer is 17 : 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

Percentage change is calculated on the original base value. If a value is p% more than a base x, the new value becomes x × (100 + p)/100.

Ratio & Proportion

A ratio compares values of the same unit. When finding the ratio of two variables expressed in terms of a common third variable, the third variable cancels out completely.

Successive Percentage

If two successive percentage changes a% and b% occur on a number, the net percentage change is given by the formula (a + b + a × b / 100)%.
</p

questions.question: Ravi decided to cover a distance of 24 km in 2 hours 24 minutes. Further he decided to cover the initial one-third of the total distance at 8 km/hr and the remaining at some different speed. What is the speed (in km/hr) of Ravi after one-third distance is covered?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 2 + 24/60 = 12/5 hours.

Time to cover first 8 km (1/3rd of 24) at 8 km/hr = 8 ÷ 8 = 1 hour.

Remaining time = 12/5 − 1 = 7/5 hours.

Remaining distance = 24 − 8 = 16 km.

Required speed = Distance ÷ Time = 16 ÷ (7/5) = 80/7 = 11 3/7 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 3/7 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 24 km

Total time = 2 hours 24 minutes

Speed for initial 1/3rd distance = 8 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 

 Total Distance = 24 km
 

 8 km
 

 16 km
 
• 
 
 
 
 
• 
 Speed = 8 km/hr
 Time = 1 hr
 Speed = ? km/hr
 Time = 7/5 hr
 

 Total Time = 2 hr 24 min (12/5 hr)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total time = 2 + (24/60) hours = 2 + 2/5 = 12/5 hours

⇒ Initial 1/3rd distance = 24 × 1/3 = 8 km

⇒ Time taken for initial distance = 8 ÷ 8 = 1 hour

⇒ Remaining distance = 24 − 8 = 16 km

⇒ Remaining time = Total time − Initial time

⇒ Remaining time = 12/5 − 1 = (12 − 5)/5 = 7/5 hours

⇒ Speed for remaining distance = Remaining distance ÷ Remaining time

⇒ Speed = 16 ÷ (7/5) = (16 × 5) / 7 = 80/7 km/hr

⇒ Speed = 11 3/7 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 11 3/7 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance covered divided by the total time taken. If equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, average speed = (2xy)/(x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = (S₁ − S₂). In opposite directions, relative speed = (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: While selling 15 balls for ₹1,220, there is loss equal to the cost price of 5 balls. The cost price (in ₹) of one ball is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss = CP of 15 balls − SP of 15 balls

CP of 5 balls = CP of 15 balls − ₹1,220

15 CP − 5 CP = ₹1,220 ⇒ 10 CP = ₹1,220

CP of 1 ball = ₹1,220 ÷ 10 = ₹122

**∴ The correct answer is ₹122.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) of 15 balls = ₹1,220

Loss incurred = Cost Price (CP) of 5 balls

**Formula Used:**

Loss = Total Cost Price (CP) − Total Selling Price (SP)

 
 
 
• 
 
 10 × CP
 5 × CP
 
 

 SP of 15 balls = ₹1,220
 
 

 Loss = 5 × CP

 

 Total Cost Price of 15 balls = 15 × CP
 
 10 × CP = 1220 ⇒ 1 CP = ₹122

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of one ball be ₹x.

⇒ Total CP of 15 balls = ₹15x

⇒ Loss incurred on selling 15 balls = CP of 5 balls = ₹5x

⇒ Loss = Total CP − Total SP

⇒ 5x = 15x − 1220

⇒ 15x − 5x = 1220

⇒ 10x = 1220

⇒ x = 1220 ÷ 10

⇒ x = 122

**∴ The correct answer is ₹122.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when Selling Price > Cost Price (Profit = SP − CP). Loss occurs when Cost Price > Selling Price (Loss = CP − SP). All calculations are strictly based on the Cost Price.

Profit / Loss Percentage

Both Profit % and Loss % are always calculated relative to the Cost Price: Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Equating Quantities Rule

When SP of 'a' articles equals CP of 'b' articles, the overall Profit or Loss % can be calculated directly using: ((b − a) ÷ a) × 100.

questions.question: The students in the three sections A, B and C of Class X are in the ratio 5 : 4 : 7. If 15, 16 and 9 new students are admitted to sections A, B and C, respectively, the ratio changes to 10 : 9 : 11. What is the total number of students in Class X after the new admissions?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the final number of students in sections A, B, and C be 10y, 9y, and 11y.

The initial students in sections A and B were (10y − 15) and (9y − 16).

Equating these to their initial ratio: (10y − 15) / (9y − 16) = 5 / 4

⇒ 40y − 60 = 45y − 80 ⇒ 5y = 20 ⇒ y = 4

Total new students = 10y + 9y + 11y = 30y = 30 × 4 = 120.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial ratio of students in sections A, B, and C = 5 : 4 : 7

New students admitted to A, B, and C = 15, 16, and 9 respectively.

Final ratio of students after admissions = 10 : 9 : 11

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial number of students in sections A, B, and C be 5x, 4x, and 7x respectively.

⇒ After the new admissions, students in A = 5x + 15

⇒ Students in B = 4x + 16

⇒ Students in C = 7x + 9

⇒ According to the new ratio for sections A and B:

⇒ (5x + 15) / (4x + 16) = 10 / 9

⇒ 9 × (5x + 15) = 10 × (4x + 16)

⇒ 45x + 135 = 40x + 160

⇒ 45x − 40x = 160 − 135

⇒ 5x = 25 ⇒ x = 5

⇒ Now, substitute x = 5 to find the final number of students in each section:

⇒ Final students in A = 5(5) + 15 = 40

⇒ Final students in B = 4(5) + 16 = 36

⇒ Final students in C = 7(5) + 9 = 44

⇒ Total final number of students = 40 + 36 + 44 = 120

**∴ The correct answer is 120 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio & Proportion

If a : b = c : d, then a × d = b × c. This cross-multiplication method is universally applied to solve unknown terms in given proportions.

Direct Multiple Check Trick

When asked for a total based on a final ratio, the total must mathematically be a strict multiple of the sum of the final ratio parts (e.g., 10 + 9 + 11 = 30). Checking options for multiples of 30 can often eliminate incorrect choices instantly.

Compound Ratio

When multiple independent ratios are combined together, the compound ratio is simply the product of antecedent terms to the product of consequent terms, written as (a × c) : (b × d).

questions.question: The population of a district is 327000, out of which 224000 are males. 65% of the population is literate. If 65% males are literate, then what percentage of females are literate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the weighted average concept, if the overall percentage equals the percentage of one component, the other component must also have the exact same percentage.

The overall literacy rate of the district is 65%.

The literacy rate among males is also given as 65%.

Therefore, to maintain this identical overall average, the female literacy rate must also be exactly 65%.

**∴ The correct answer is 65%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total population = 327000

Male population = 224000

Overall literate percentage = 65%

Male literate percentage = 65%

**Formula Used:**

Total Literate Population = Literate Males + Literate Females

**Calculations:**

⇒ Female population = Total population − Male population

⇒ Female population = 327000 − 224000 = 103000

⇒ Total literate population = 65% of 327000

⇒ Total literates = (65 ÷ 100) × 327000 = 212550

⇒ Literate males = 65% of 224000

⇒ Literate males = (65 ÷ 100) × 224000 = 145600

⇒ Literate females = Total literates − Literate males

⇒ Literate females = 212550 − 145600 = 66950

⇒ Percentage of literate females = (Literate females ÷ Female population) × 100

⇒ % Literate females = (66950 ÷ 103000) × 100

⇒ % Literate females = 6695 ÷ 103 = 65%

**∴ The correct answer is 65%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Logic

When a population is divided into two groups, if one group shares the exact same percentage or average as the entire combined population, the second group must inevitably share that identical percentage to keep the balance.

Alligation Method

A fast technique to find the ratio of components in a mixture. The ratio of quantities is derived using cross-differences: |A₂ − Aw| : |Aw − A₁|, where Aw is the weighted average.

Percentage Calculation

To calculate what percentage a specific part represents out of a whole, always use the formula: (Part Value ÷ Total Base Value) × 100. Always ensure the base value corresponds to the specific group in question (e.g., total females).
</p

questions.question: Yogesh invested some money in HDFC at 4% per annum rate of interest. What would be the corresponding simple interest (in ₹) if after 2 years, Yogesh got ₹229.5 as compound interest, considering annual compounding?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of CI for 2 years = R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100

Effective CI rate = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4) ÷ 100 = 8.16%

Effective SI rate = 4 × 2 = 8%

Given, 8.16% corresponds to → ₹229.5

SI (8%) = (229.5 ÷ 8.16) × 8 = ₹225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate (R) = 4% per annum, Time (T) = 2 years, Compound Interest (CI) = ₹229.5

**Formula Used:**

CI = P × [(1 + R/100)² − 1]

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Principal (100%)
 
 
• 
 
•

 Year 2 SI: 4%

 
• 
 4% of 4%

 Total SI = 8%
 Total CI = 8.16%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the principal be P.

⇒ 229.5 = P × [(1 + 4/100)² − 1]

⇒ 229.5 = P × [(1 + 1/25)² − 1]

⇒ 229.5 = P × [(26/25)² − 1]

⇒ 229.5 = P × [676/625 − 1]

⇒ 229.5 = P × (51/625)

⇒ P = (229.5 × 625) ÷ 51

⇒ P = 4.5 × 625 = ₹2812.5

⇒ Now, Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (2812.5 × 4 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 22500 ÷ 100 = ₹225

**∴ The correct answer is ₹225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective CI Rate for 2 Years

The effective compound interest rate for two years at R% per annum can be directly calculated using the successive percentage formula: 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

Direct Relation Between SI and CI for 2 Years

For a given principal and rate, the direct relationship between Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years is defined as CI = SI × (1 + R ÷ 200).

Difference Between CI and SI for 2 Years

The exact numerical difference between compound interest and simple interest on a principal P for 2 years at rate R% is evaluated using the formula: Diff = P × (R ÷ 100)².

questions.question: A merchant fixes the marked price of his goods at 50% above the cost price. He sells his goods at 12% discount. His percentage of profit is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The successive percentage formula can be directly used to find the net profit percentage.

Net Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup % × Discount %) ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 50 − 12 − (50 × 12) ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 38 − 600 ÷ 100

Net Profit % = 38 − 6 = 32%

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 CP = 100
 
 
 MP = 150
 
 
 SP = 132
 
 

 +50% Markup
 
 

 −12% Discount
 
 

 +32% Profit
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

**Given:**

Markup percentage = 50% above CP

Discount percentage = 12% on MP

**Formulas Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 + Markup %) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 50% of 100 = 150

⇒ Discount = 12% of MP

⇒ Discount = (12 ÷ 100) × 150 = 18

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

⇒ SP = 150 − 18 = 132

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 132 − 100 = 32

⇒ Profit % = (32 ÷ 100) × 100 = 32%

**∴ The correct answer is 32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed or tagged on an article is called its marked price. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price or Selling Price.

Relation between CP and MP

A direct relationship ratio between CP and MP is: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount %) ÷ (100 + Profit %).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.
</p

questions.question: Two trains having lengths of 210 m and 440 m are running at speeds of 60 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance to cross = Sum of train lengths = 210 + 440 = 650 m.

Relative speed (same direction) = 90 − 60 = 30 km/h.

Convert relative speed to m/s = 30 × (5 / 18) = 25 / 3 m/s.

Time to cross = Distance ÷ Speed = 650 × (3 / 25) = 78 seconds.

Time in minutes = 78 ÷ 60 = 1.3 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Total Relative Distance = 210 + 440 = 650 m
 
 Trains Moving in Same Direction

**Given:**

Length of slower train (L₁) = 210 m

Length of faster train (L₂) = 440 m

Speed of slower train (V₁) = 60 km/h

Speed of faster train (V₂) = 90 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = V₂ − V₁

Time to cross = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 210 + 440 = 650 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 90 − 60 = 30 km/h

⇒ Convert speed to m/s = 30 × (5 / 18) = 150 / 18 = 25 / 3 m/s

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 650 ÷ (25 / 3) = 650 × (3 / 25)

⇒ Time taken = 26 × 3 = 78 seconds

⇒ Convert time to minutes = 78 ÷ 60 = 1.3 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 1.3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (V₁ − V₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂).

Trains Crossing

When a train completely crosses another train (whether moving or stationary) or a platform, the total distance covered to clear each other is always the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by (5 / 18). Conversely, to convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 / 5).
</p

questions.question: Rakesh sold 150 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 75 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 chair be 1 unit.

Total SP = 150 units, Profit = SP of 75 chairs = 75 units.

Cost Price (CP) = Total SP − Profit = 150 − 75 = 75 units.

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (75 ÷ 75) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of chairs sold = 150

Gain = Selling Price (SP) of 75 chairs

**Formula Used:**

Gain = SP − Cost Price (CP)

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total SP of 150 chairs = 150 units

 
 
 CP = 75 units

 
 
 Profit = 75 units

 
 Profit % = (75 ÷ 75) × 100 = 100%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the Selling Price of 1 chair be 1 unit.

⇒ Total SP of 150 chairs = 150 × 1 = 150 units

⇒ Gain = SP of 75 chairs = 75 × 1 = 75 units

⇒ We know that CP = SP − Gain

⇒ CP of 150 chairs = 150 − 75 = 75 units

⇒ Substitute CP and Gain values into the formula to find Gain % :

⇒ Gain % = (75 ÷ 75) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 1 × 100 = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when Selling Price > Cost Price. Profit = SP − CP. Loss occurs when Cost Price > Selling Price. Loss = CP − SP.

Profit/Loss Percentage

Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) as the base, unless the question explicitly specifies otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, the actual profit percentage is given by: Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
</p

questions.question: A cube of side 9 cm made of iron is melted and recast into 8 small cubes. Find the side (in cm) of each small cube.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When melting and recasting, the total volume remains constant.

Volume ratio of Large Cube to One Small Cube = 8 : 1

Side ratio = (Volume ratio)¹/³ = (8)¹/³ : (1)¹/³ = 2 : 1

The side of the large cube represents 2 parts = 9 cm.

Therefore, the side of the small cube (1 part) = 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 
 

 

 

 9 cm

•

 a cm
 
 × 8 Small Cubes

**Given:**

⇒ Side of the large cube = 9 cm

⇒ Number of small cubes formed = 8

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Volume of a cube = (Side)³

⇒ Total volume before melting = Total volume after recasting

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the large iron cube = 9 × 9 × 9 = 729 cm³

⇒ The large cube is melted into 8 equal small cubes.

⇒ Let the side of each small cube be a cm.

⇒ Volume of 8 small cubes = 8 × a³

⇒ 8 × a³ = 729

⇒ a³ = 729 ÷ 8

⇒ a = (729 ÷ 8)¹/³

⇒ a = 9 ÷ 2

⇒ a = 4.5 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4.5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conservation of Volume

When any 3D object is melted and recast into another shape (or multiple smaller objects), the total volume remains constant, while the total surface area usually increases.

Cube Properties

Volume of a cube = a³
Total Surface Area (TSA) = 6a²
Diagonal of a cube = a√3

Ratio Theorem for 3D Shapes

If two similar 3D objects have a side/radius ratio of a : b, their corresponding surface area ratio is a² : b², and their volume ratio is a³ : b³.
</p

questions.question: 12 chairs and 6 tables were bought for ₹12,600. If the average cost of a table is ₹1,500, then find the average cost of a chair.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total cost of 12 chairs = Total amount − Total cost of 6 tables

Total cost of 12 chairs = 12600 − (6 × 1500)

Total cost of 12 chairs = 12600 − 9000 = 3600

Average cost of 1 chair = 3600 ÷ 12 = 300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total cost of 12 chairs and 6 tables = ₹12,600

Average cost of a table = ₹1,500

**Formula Used:**

Total Cost = Average Cost × Quantity
